name: The Great Camphor of Zhishan Rock

location.address: Zhishan Rock Cultural History Park, near Yunong Library (雨農圖書館), Zhicheng Rd Sec 2 area, Shilin District, Taipei

access: Free entry. Inside Zhishan Rock Cultural History Park (芝山岩文化史蹟公園), a public hillside park and historic site open daily with no admission fee (note: the adjacent ticketed Zhishan Culture and Ecology Garden, NT$50, is a separate enclosed section nearby; this tree stands in the free trail/park area near Yunong Library, not inside that paid garden, per the sources describing it as beside the library on the open trail).
transport: Zhishan MRT Station (Red Line, Danshui-Xinyi), exit 1, roughly 8-10 minute walk via Zhicheng Rd and the trail entrance; alternatively approach via the Yunong Bridge riverside parking area and the 120-step Bai'erkan (百二崁) staircase.
verify_notes: Two independent sources both describe a single ancient camphor tree standing near Yunong Library/Reading Room (雨農圖書館/雨農閱覽室) on Zhishan Rock, called locally the oldest tree in Taipei. hopeintw.org.tw gives 'roughly 300 years' (三百年的大樟木); hiking.biji.co gives approximately 320 years and calls it explicitly 台北市最老的樹 (Taipei's oldest tree) -- ages not identical, both kept as the honest range, do not sharpen to one figure. Historically notable: hiking.biji.co states six Japanese teachers killed in the 1895 Zhishan Rock Incident were buried beneath this large camphor tree (合葬在山上大樟樹下) -- strong 'witnessed history' hook for the story. Zhishan Rock was designated a protected forest (保安林) under Japanese rule, which is why old-growth camphor survived here when most native camphor elsewhere was logged for camphor oil. No girth figure found in either source. Exact tree-level GPS not found; coordinates given are for Zhishan Rock generally (25.103846, 121.530295 per zh.wikipedia infobox), nudged toward the library area -- treat as park-level, not trunk-level. A third source, culture.gov.taipei's own page for the adjacent Zhishan Culture and Ecology Garden, was fetched directly and does NOT mention this camphor tree at all, which is consistent with the tree standing in the free trail area outside that ticketed garden rather than inside it -- worth confirming on a future pass with eyes on the ground or a satellite check.

name: The Common Three Pines

location.address: In front of the Common Teaching Building (共同教學館), National Taiwan University main campus, near Zhoushan Road / Luming Plaza, Da'an District, Taipei

access: Free. Open university campus with no gate or admission fee; the pines stand on a public plaza in front of a teaching building that students, staff and visitors walk through freely.
transport: NTU main campus; roughly 10-15 minute walk from Gongguan MRT Station (Songshan-Xindian Line) or Taipower Building MRT Station.
verify_notes: Three Ryukyu pines (Pinus luchuensis) in front of NTU's Common Teaching Building, collectively nicknamed 'Common Three Pines' (共同三松) and voted one of NTU's Twelve Scenic Spots (台大十二景) in a 2005 student poll -- confirms this is a named, recognised specimen, not just background planting (zh.wikipedia, directly fetched). Two of the three are individually listed on Taipei's city protected-tree register, ids 10615-00047 and 10615-00048 (per zh.wikipedia; register page itself not independently fetched this pass, could not find a working query URL for eculturedata.gov.taipei -- see host notes). Age: a 2010-2011 estimate put the trees at approximately 80 years old, which derives to roughly 95 years old by 2026; kept as a broad band rather than a sharp number. The Common Teaching Building's floor plan was deliberately recessed / set back to accommodate the pines as they grew, and NTU built an elevated wooden boardwalk platform around the trio -- a good visual/story detail. raywang1016.pixnet.net (an independent campus-tour blog, fetched directly) confirms the pines are still standing today and are a popular student rest spot near food vendors. No girth figure found. Exact tree-level coordinates not found; used an estimate near the Common Teaching Building based on its position relative to NTU's Comprehensive Teaching Building (25.018243, 121.539409, confirmed via search), nudged toward Zhoushan Road -- flag as approximate, a future pass should pin this from a campus map or satellite image.

name: The Presidential Junipers of Taipei Confucius Temple

location.address: Qingyun Road (青雲路), between the Pan Pond (泮池) and the Lingxing Gate (欞星門), Taipei Confucius Temple, 275 Dalong St, Datong District, Taipei

access: Free entry. Taipei Confucius Temple is a public temple and municipal historic monument open to visitors daily (typical hours are morning to early evening; confirm current opening times locally). Sits directly beside Bao'an Temple (保安宮) in the Dalongdong cultural district, an easy joint walk.
transport: Roughly 10 minute walk from Yuanshan MRT Station (Red Line); several bus routes stop at Hami St / Dalongdong.
verify_notes: Two Chinese junipers (龍柏) planted on Qingyun Road, the path between the Pan Pond and the Lingxing Gate, by then-President Chiang Kai-shek and Vice President Chen Cheng on Arbor Day (12 March) 1962 -- a documented planting date, not an estimate, so age is exact rather than derived. Confirmed by zh.wikipedia (directly fetched): trees were transplanted about 1 metre during a 2011 Ming Lun Hall renovation and are described as still standing in the temple grounds today. wenshuh2004.pixnet.net (independent blog, directly fetched) corroborates the same location and 1962 planting story and separately confirms 2011 renovation work at the site. A separate WebSearch (not independently fetched, treat as a lead only) mentioned commemorative inscription stones reading '總統蔣中正手植' and '副總統陳誠手植' dated to ROC year 51 (1962) -- plausible and consistent with the confirmed facts, but not itself verified by a direct source fetch this pass. A second pair of junipers was also planted in 1955 by the same two officials in front of Ming Lun Hall nearby -- a possible additional/companion candidate for a future pass, not researched further here (same temple grounds, would not add walking distance). This is not an ancient tree -- the case for it is historical significance (heads of state, a fixed and unusually well-documented planting date) rather than raw age, and it forms a natural two-stop cluster with Bao'an Temple next door. Address and coordinates are temple-grounds level from Wikipedia's infobox, not a pin on the tree itself -- approximate.

name: The Ginkgo of the Geology Building

location.address: In front of the Geology Science Building (地質科學館), National Taiwan University main campus, near Zhoushan Road, Da'an District, Taipei

access: Free. Open university campus with no gate or admission fee.
transport: NTU main campus; roughly 10-15 minute walk from Gongguan MRT Station (Songshan-Xindian Line) or Taipower Building MRT Station. Close to the Common Three Pines (tpe_002), an easy joint stop on the same campus walk.
verify_notes: A ginkgo tree stands in front of NTU's Geology Science Building alongside a dawn redwood (水杉), both informally described as 'living fossil' specimens -- confirmed by raywang1016.pixnet.net (independent campus-tour blog, directly fetched): '地質系館門口有活化石銀杏跟水杉'. Ginkgo is rare in lowland Taiwan and this specimen is noted for turning gold later than usual (not until winter/January) because of the low-elevation heat. AGE UNRESOLVED, deliberately left blank rather than guessed: a WebSearch synthesis (NOT independently fetched -- source pages were 403-blocked or unreachable this pass, see host notes) claimed both that the tree is 'over 40 years old' and, separately, that it was 'planted by a Japanese person' and is one of Taipei's registered protected trees under id 10615-00010 -- which would imply a pre-1945 planting and 80+ years, not 40. These two claims contradict each other and neither was seen on a directly fetched page, so per the search-summary-is-a-lead rule neither goes in age_estimate. A future pass should fetch the actual register entry (eculturedata.gov.taipei blocks the query API with a 403 'insufficient permission' from this environment; a browser session may get further) or a directly-loadable NTU/news source before setting an age. Existence, species and location are solid; age is the open question. No girth figure found. Coordinates are an estimate for the general NTU old-campus core, not a tree-level pin.
